chial hyperreactivity—tendency of the 
smooth muscle of the tracheobronchial tree to
narrow in response to a stimulus; present 
in virtually all symptomatic patients with 
asthma
bronchitis—a condition characterized by inﬂ am-
mation and eventual scarring of the lining of
the bronchial tubes accompanied by restricted
airﬂ ow, excessive mucus production, and a 
persistent cough
bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD)—a chronic
lung disorder that may affect infants who have
been exposed to high levels of oxygen therapy
and ventilator support
chest physiotherapy—physical therapy that
includes a variety of techniques designed to
reduce or prevent infection by clearing pooled
secretions and/or infected materials from the
lungs
chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 
(COPD)—a disease that limits airﬂ ow through 
either inﬂ ammation of the lining of the bronchial 
tubes or destruction of alveoli
clubbing—changes in ﬁ ngers and toes due to 
hypoxemia; ﬁ ngers and toes show a curve at a
tip of the nail with ﬂ attening surface
cor pulmonale—an increase in size of the right
ventricle of the heart caused by resistance to
the passage of blood through the lungs; can lead
to heart failure
cyanosis—blue-tinged mucous membranes and
skin due to inadequate oxygen supply
cystic ﬁ brosis (CF)—disease characterized by
abnormally thick mucus secretions from the
epithelial surfaces of various organ systems,
including the respiratory tract, the gastrointesti-
nal tract, the liver, the genitourinary system, and
the sweat glands
dyspnea—shortness of breath or difﬁ culty 
breathing
